faqs.question: How long does the course take?
faqs.answer: Most undergraduate courses take 3-4 years of full-time study. Postgraduate taught courses typically take 1-2 years, while research degrees (PhD) can take 3-4 years.

faqs.question: How much are the tuition fees?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees vary by course and level of study. UK undergraduate fees are typically capped at £9,250 per year, while international and postgraduate fees can be higher.

faqs.question: What are the entry requirements?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements vary by course. Most undergraduate courses require A-levels or equivalent qualifications, typically AAA-BBB. Postgraduate courses usually require a 2:1 bachelor's degree.

faqs.question: Is the course available full-time or part-time?
faqs.answer: Many courses are available in both full-time and part-time formats. Full-time study is typically 3-4 years, while part-time study takes longer but offers flexibility.

faqs.question: Can I study this course online?
faqs.answer: Some courses are available as distance learning or online programmes. This allows students to study from anywhere with flexible scheduling.

faqs.question: What is the cost of student accommodation?
faqs.answer: Student accommodation costs vary by location and room type. Typically, university halls range from £100-£250 per week depending on the city and facilities.

faqs.question: What types of accommodation are available?
faqs.answer: Universities offer a range of accommodation options including en-suite rooms, shared bathrooms, studio flats, and family housing. On-campus halls are the most common for first-year students.

faqs.question: How far is the accommodation from campus?
faqs.answer: University accommodation is typically located on or near campus, usually within a 15-20 minute walk. Private housing may be further away but often cheaper.

faqs.question: When should I apply for accommodation?
faqs.answer: It is recommended to apply for accommodation as early as possible. Most universities open accommodation applications in spring for the following academic year.

faqs.question: What study modes are available for postgraduate courses?
faqs.answer: Postgraduate courses are typically available in full-time, part-time, and sometimes distance learning formats. Full-time MSc/MA programmes usually take 1 year.

faqs.question: Are scholarships available?
faqs.answer: Many universities offer scholarships, bursaries, and financial aid packages based on academic merit, background, or financial need. Check the university's funding page for details.

faqs.question: What is the difference between undergraduate and postgraduate study?
faqs.answer: Undergraduate study (e.g., bachelor's degrees) is the first level of higher education. Postgraduate study (master's, PhD) builds on a bachelor's degree and involves more specialised, advanced learning.

faqs.question: What subjects can I study?
faqs.answer: Universities offer courses across a wide range of subject areas including sciences, engineering, humanities, business, medicine, and the arts.

faqs.question: Are sandwich courses or placement years available?
faqs.answer: Some courses offer a sandwich year or work placement, typically taken between the second and final year. This provides valuable industry experience.

faqs.question: What English language tests are accepted and what scores do I need?
faqs.answer: Most universities accept IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic and Cambridge English. For postgraduate study a typical requirement is IELTS 6.0-6.5 overall with no band below 5.5-6.0, though requirements vary by course.

faqs.question: Are KCSE qualifications accepted for entry?
faqs.answer: Many UK universities accept KCSE for foundation or undergraduate entry, often with specific grade requirements. Check the university's country-specific page for Kenya for the exact KCSE grade equivalences.

faqs.question: Do international students need a student visa to study in the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes, most international students need a Student visa (formerly Tier 4). You will need a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your university, proof of funds, and English language evidence.

faqs.question: What documents do I need to submit with my application?
faqs.answer: Applications typically require academic transcripts and certificates, English test results, a personal statement, reference letters, a copy of your passport, and proof of funding where applicable.

faqs.question: When should I apply and what are the deadlines?
faqs.answer: It is recommended to apply 6-12 months before your intended start date. Many postgraduate courses accept applications up to the start of term, but popular courses fill early and scholarship deadlines are often much earlier.

faqs.question: Can international students work while studying?
faqs.answer: On a Student visa you may usually work up to 20 hours per week during term time and full-time during holidays, subject to your visa conditions.

faqs.question: How do international students pay tuition fees?
faqs.answer: Tuition fees can usually be paid in full or in instalments via bank transfer, international cards, or through approved agents. Some universities offer early-payment discounts.

faqs.question: What is the cost of living for international students in the UK?
faqs.answer: Living costs typically range from £1,000 to £1,500 per month depending on the city, covering accommodation, food, transport and personal expenses. London and the South East are generally more expensive.

faqs.question: Can I apply before I receive my final results or passport?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can apply with predicted grades or a conditional offer. A valid passport is needed for the visa application, but universities can issue a conditional offer before it is ready.

faqs.question: What happens if I have a study gap in my education?
faqs.answer: Universities may ask you to explain any study gap. Provide evidence of work, volunteering or other productive activity during the gap to strengthen your application.

faqs.question: Are there scholarships or bursaries for Kenyan international students?
faqs.answer: Many universities offer merit-based scholarships, country-specific awards and early-application discounts for international students. Check the university's funding and scholarship pages for eligibility and deadlines.

faqs.question: What KCSE English grade do I need for Aston University?
faqs.answer: For entry onto an undergraduate or postgraduate taught degree, a minimum Grade of C is acceptable from English Language in the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE). For the MBChB medicine course, you need a minimum of Grade B in English.

faqs.question: I finished KCSE and want to do a foundation year - what do I need?
faqs.answer: For the International Foundation Year you need 12 years of study and an average of five subjects at grade C and above in KCSE, and the subjects must include the relevant subjects for your course.

faqs.question: What do I need to get onto a Masters at Aston from Kenya?
faqs.answer: You need a recognised Bachelor's honours second class (upper) degree. Aston can also consider a second class (lower) degree for some courses on a case-by-case basis if you have relevant industry experience.

faqs.question: I got a second class lower degree but I have work experience - can I still do a Masters?
faqs.answer: Yes, possibly. Aston can consider a Bachelor's honours second class (lower) degree for some courses on a case-by-case basis, especially if you have relevant industry experience.

faqs.question: Can I combine two scholarships at Aston?
faqs.answer: No. Aston scholarships cannot be combined - you are awarded the highest value scholarship available to you.

faqs.question: What study background do I need for undergraduate entry at Aston?
faqs.answer: You need 13 years of study, or 12 years plus a Diploma, a recognised Foundation programme, Cambridge A-Level, International Baccalaureate, BTech or HND.

faqs.question: How much is the postgraduate scholarship at BCU and who can get it?
faqs.answer: BCU is offering a scholarship of £3,000 to self-funding international postgraduate students joining on a full-time postgraduate taught Master's degree. It is applied as a tuition fee discount.

faqs.question: Is there an undergraduate scholarship at BCU?
faqs.answer: Yes, BCU is offering a scholarship of £5,000 to self-funding international undergraduate students.

faqs.question: Do I need IELTS if I did KCSE English?
faqs.answer: BCU accepts the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) as evidence of English language. Check the individual scores required and the full list of accepted English qualifications on BCU's accepted qualifications and English tests page.

faqs.question: What IELTS score do most BCU courses require?
faqs.answer: Most courses require IELTS 6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in each band, or equivalent, but some courses do have a higher requirement - check the individual course page.

faqs.question: I only have a KCSE certificate - can I apply for undergraduate entry at BCU?
faqs.answer: Yes, BCU accepts students who hold a KCSE certificate for undergraduate entry.

faqs.question: What class of degree do I need for a Masters at RGU from Kenya?
faqs.answer: You need a 4-year degree with a minimum of a second class lower classification with 50% or Grade C, or a Credit. A small number of postgraduate programmes do require a minimum of second class upper classification - refer to the relevant course page.

faqs.question: I got 50% in my degree - am I eligible for a Masters at RGU?
faqs.answer: Yes for most programmes. A 4-year degree with a minimum of a second class lower classification (50% or Grade C, or a Credit) meets the postgraduate requirement, although a small number of programmes need a second class upper instead.

faqs.question: What IELTS score do I need for postgraduate study at RGU?
faqs.answer: Postgraduate courses at RGU require IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 in each area. Some courses require a higher score, so always check the course page.

faqs.question: I got a C in KCSE English - is that enough for RGU?
faqs.answer: For most courses, yes. RGU accepts KCSE English at grade C as the equivalent to an IELTS 6.5/6.0. Some courses have exceptions - check the English language requirements page.

faqs.question: What IELTS score do undergraduate courses at RGU need?
faqs.answer: Most undergraduate courses require an IELTS score of 6.0, with a minimum of 5.5 in each area.

faqs.question: What KCSE grades do I need for a foundation year at UCLan?
faqs.answer: For the foundation year you need Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) Grade B average in 5 or more subjects.

faqs.question: I have a Kenya Diploma - can I start in Year 1 at UCLan?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Kenya Diploma awarded by the Kenya National Examinations Council with a grade of 60% or above meets the Undergraduate (Year 1) entry requirement.

faqs.question: What do I need for a Masters at UCLan from Kenya?
faqs.answer: You need a minimum 2:2 in a bachelor degree from a recognised institution in a relevant subject.

faqs.question: What IELTS score does UCLan require?
faqs.answer: The standard English language entry requirement is IELTS 6.0 with no component score lower than 5.5, or equivalent.

faqs.question: My degree is a 2:2 but not in the same subject as the Masters I want - can I apply?
faqs.answer: The postgraduate requirement at UCLan is a minimum 2:2 in a bachelor degree from a recognised institution in a relevant subject, so the degree subject needs to be relevant to the course you want to study.
